exposure: race and ethnicity (non-Hispanic Black vs. non-Hispanic White)
outcome: severe maternal morbidity (SMM) without blood transfusion
cohort: The study included individuals with Medicaid insurance who experienced live births in 49 US states and Washington, DC between 2016 and 2018.
finding: The study found significant state-level and racial/ethnic variation in delivery-related severe maternal morbidity (SMM) rates among individuals with Medicaid insurance, with non-Hispanic Black individuals experiencing a nearly 70% higher rate of SMM compared to non-Hispanic White individuals.
